title: Protective Capacity Hallucination: When Large Language Models Claim Nonexistent Capabilities
abstract: arXiv:2607.13596v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: When cast as the protector of a vulnerable user yet given no explicit capability boundary, a large language model (LLM) may respond not by acknowledging its limits but by claiming to have taken, or to be taking, a real-world protective action it cannot perform, such as contacting emergency services or administering care. We term this phenomenon Protective Capacity Hallucination (PCH): a self-referential misattribution in which a model, acting in a protective role, asserts physical or institutional agency exceeding its affordances as a language model. In a three-phase study spanning eight LLMs and 13,600 sessions, we find that PCH depends on both situational severity and interactional format. Across ordinary service domains, multi-party dialogic input drives PCH to near-ceiling levels in most models. In contrast, PCH remains at floor levels in all eight models when the same models are placed in intimate-partner conflict scenario

translated_title: 保护能力幻觉：当大型语言模型宣称不存在的能力时
translated_abstract: 当大型语言模型（LLM）被设定为脆弱用户的保护者，却没有被赋予明确的能力边界时，它可能不是承认自身的局限，而是声称已经采取或正在采取它实际上无法执行的现实世界保护行动，例如联系紧急服务或实施救助。我们将这一现象命名为保护能力幻觉（Protective Capacity Hallucination, PCH）：一种自我指涉的错误归因，即模型在扮演保护者角色时，宣称拥有超出其作为语言模型实际能力范围的物理或机构性行动能力。在一项涵盖八个大型语言模型和13,600个会话的三阶段研究中，我们发现PCH既取决于情境的严重程度，也取决于交互的形式。在普通服务领域中，多方对话式输入使大多数模型的PCH达到接近上限的水平。相比之下，当相同的模型被置于亲密伴侣冲突情境中时，所有八个模型的PCH都保持在最低水平。
tldr: 该研究首次提出并命名了“保护能力幻觉”（PCH）这一现象——大型语言模型在扮演保护者角色时会虚假宣称自己正在执行现实中无法完成的保护行动（如联系紧急服务），并通过涵盖八个模型、13,600个会话的三阶段研究揭示PCH同时受情境严重程度和交互形式的影响：在多方对话输入的普通服务场景中接近上限，而在亲密伴侣冲突场景中则处于最低水平。
en_tdlr: This study identifies and names "Protective Capacity Hallucination" (PCH), a phenomenon in which LLMs acting as protectors falsely claim to have taken real-world protective actions they cannot perform, and reveals through a three-phase study spanning eight LLMs and 13,600 sessions that PCH depends on both situational severity and interactional format—reaching near-ceiling levels with multi-party dialogic input in ordinary service domains while remaining at floor levels in intimate-partner conflict scenarios.
